sanskrit: ta ete muditā nityam avadhyāḥ sarvadaivataiḥ nivasanty atra rājendra gatodvegā nirutsukāḥ mānuṣo mṛtyur eteṣāṃ nirdiṣṭo brahmaṇā purā
english: These beings dwell here ever joyful, invincible to all the gods, O king of kings — free from anxiety and desire; death by a mortal hand was ordained for them by Brahmā of old.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca surāsurair avadhyāṃs tān ahaṃ jñātvā tataḥ prabho abruvaṃ mātaliṃ hṛṣṭo yāhy etat puram añjasā
english: Arjuna said: Learning that they could not be slain by gods or demons, O lord, I joyfully said to Matali, "Drive straight into that city."

sanskrit: tridaśeśadviṣo yāvat kṣayam astrair nayāmy aham na kathaṃ cid dhi me pāpā na vadhyā ye suradviṣaḥ
english: "Until I bring destruction upon the enemies of the lord of the thirty gods with my weapons, these sinful foes of the gods shall surely not escape being slain by me."

sanskrit: uvāha māṃ tataḥ śīghraṃ hiraṇyapuram antikāt rathena tena divyena hariyuktena mātaliḥ
english: Then Matali swiftly bore me close to Hiraṇyapura in that divine chariot yoked with bay horses.

sanskrit: te mām ālakṣya daiteyā vicitrābharaṇāmbarāḥ samutpetur mahāvegā rathān āsthāya daṃśitāḥ
english: Seeing me, the Daityas, clad in splendid ornaments and garments, armour-clad, mounted their chariots and rushed forth with great speed.

sanskrit: tato nālīkanārācair bhallaśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ abhyaghnan dānavendrā māṃ kruddhās tīvraparākramāḥ
english: Then the foremost of Dānavas, fierce in might and enraged, struck me with nālikā arrows, nārācas, bhallaas, śaktis, ṛṣṭis, and tomaras.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ cāstravarṣeṇa mahatā pratyavārayam śastravarṣaṃ mahad rājan vidyābalam upāśritaḥ
english: I warded off that great shower of weapons with a mighty counter-shower of missiles, O king, drawing on the power of my science of arms.

sanskrit: vyāmohayaṃ ca tān sarvān rathamārgaiś caran raṇe te 'nyonyam abhisaṃmūḍhāḥ pātayanti sma dānavāḥ
english: I bewildered them all as I moved through the battle-field in chariot-manoeuvres; confused, the Dānavas began striking one another down.

sanskrit: teṣām ahaṃ vimūḍhānām anyonyam abhidhāvatām śirāṃsi viśikhair dīptair vyaharaṃ śatasaṃghaśaḥ
english: While they were thus bewildered and rushing at each other, I severed their heads in hundreds with blazing shafts.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā daiteyāḥ puram āsthāya tat punaḥ kham utpetuḥ sanagarā māyām āsthāya dānavīm
english: The Daityas, being slaughtered, re-entered that city and rose into the sky with it entire, resorting to their demonic māyā.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā pratyavārayam mārgam āvṛtya daityānāṃ gatiṃ caiṣām avārayam
english: Then I checked their path with a great shower of arrows, covering their route and blocking their flight.

sanskrit: tat puraṃ khacaraṃ divyaṃ kāmagaṃ divyavarcasam daiteyair varadānena dhāryate sma yathāsukham
english: That sky-roving, divine, wish-moving city of celestial splendour was sustained at will by the Daityas through the boon they had been granted.

sanskrit: antarbhūmau nipatitaṃ punar ūrdhvaṃ pratiṣṭhate punas tiryak prayāty āśu punar apsu nimajjati
english: It sank beneath the earth and rose again upward; it moved swiftly sideways and then plunged once more into the waters.

sanskrit: amarāvatisaṃkāśaṃ puraṃ kāmagamaṃ tu tat aham astrair bahuvidhaiḥ pratyagṛhṇaṃ narādhipa
english: That wish-moving city, resembling Amarāvatī, I countered with many kinds of missiles, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ śarajālena divyāstramuditena ca nyagṛhṇaṃ saha daiteyais tat puraṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then with a net of arrows empowered by divine weapons I seized that city together with the Daityas within it, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: vikṣataṃ cāyasair bāṇair matprayuktair ajihmagaiḥ mahīm abhyapatad rājan prabhagnaṃ puram āsuram
english: Pierced through and through by my straight-flying iron arrows, the demonic city crashed shattered to the earth, O king.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā madbāṇair vajravegair ayasmayaiḥ paryabhramanta vai rājann asurāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Struck by my iron arrows swift as thunderbolts, the asuras reeled about, O king, driven by fate.

sanskrit: tato mātalir apy āśu purastān nipatann iva mahīm avātarat kṣipraṃ rathenādityavarcasā
english: Then Matali too swiftly descended toward the earth as if swooping down, quickly landing with that sun-bright chariot.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭis teṣām amarṣiṇām yuyutsūnāṃ mayā sārdhaṃ paryavartanta bhārata
english: Then sixty thousand chariots of those indignant ones, eager to fight with me, wheeled around, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ niśitair bāṇair vyadhamaṃ gārdhravājitaiḥ te yuddhe saṃnyavartanta samudrasya yathormayaḥ
english: I pierced them with sharp arrows winged with vulture feathers; they surged back in battle like waves of the ocean.

sanskrit: neme śakyā mānuṣeṇa yuddheneti pracintya vai tato 'ham ānupūrvyeṇa sarvāṇy astrāṇy ayojayam
english: Reflecting that these could not be overcome by mortal combat alone, I then deployed all my weapons in due order.

sanskrit: tatas tāni sahasrāṇi rathānāṃ citrayodhinām astrāṇi mama divyāni pratyaghnañ śanakair iva
english: Then those thousands of chariots with their variegated warriors began, as it were, to neutralise my divine weapons one by one.

sanskrit: rathamārgān vicitrāṃs te vicaranto mahārathāḥ pratyadṛśyanta saṃgrāme śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Those great warriors, moving in intricate chariot-paths, appeared in the battle by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: vicitramukuṭāpīḍā vicitrakavacadhvajāḥ vicitrābharaṇāś caiva nandayantīva me manaḥ
english: Wearing varied diadems and crowns, varied armour and banners, and varied ornaments, they were, as it were, a delight to my heart.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu śaravarṣais tān astrapramuditai raṇe nāśaknuvaṃ pīḍayituṃ te tu māṃ paryapīḍayan
english: Yet though I poured showers of weapon-energised arrows upon them in battle, I could not afflict them — while they afflicted me greatly.

sanskrit: taiḥ pīḍyamāno bahubhiḥ kṛtāstraiḥ kuśalair yudhi vyathito 'smi mahāyuddhe bhayaṃ cāgān mahan mama
english: Hard pressed by those many skilled warriors trained in arms, I was distressed in that great battle and a great fear came over me.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ devadevāya rudrāya praṇato raṇe svasti bhūtebhya ity uktvā mahāstraṃ samayojayam yat tad raudram iti khyātaṃ sarvāmitravināśanam
english: Then, bowing in battle to Rudra, the god of gods, and uttering "May all beings be well," I invoked the great weapon known as the Raudra — the destroyer of all enemies.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ triśirasaṃ puruṣaṃ navalocanam trimukhaṃ ṣaḍbhujaṃ dīptam arkajvalanamūrdhajam lelihānair mahānāgaiḥ kṛtaśīrṣam amitrahan
english: Then I beheld a three-headed person with nine eyes, three faces, six arms, blazing, with hair like the flaming sun, his heads crowned with great serpents whose tongues flickered — the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: vibhīs tatas tad astraṃ tu ghoraṃ raudraṃ sanātanam dṛṣṭvā gāṇḍīvasaṃyogam ānīya bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing that terrible, ancient Raudra weapon take shape, I was filled with awe; bringing it to the string of Gāṇḍīva, O bull of the Bhāratas —

sanskrit: namaskṛtvā trinetrāya śarvāyāmitatejase muktavān dānavendrāṇāṃ parābhāvāya bhārata
english: — bowing to the three-eyed Śarva of boundless radiance, I released it for the defeat of the lords of the Dānavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: muktamātre tatas tasmin rūpāṇy āsan sahasraśaḥ mṛgāṇām atha siṃhānāṃ vyāghrāṇāṃ ca viśāṃ pate ṛkṣāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca pannagānāṃ tathā gavām
english: The moment it was released, thousands of forms appeared — of deer, lions, tigers, O lord of the people, bears, buffaloes, serpents, and cattle —

sanskrit: gajānāṃ sṛmarāṇāṃ ca śarabhāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ṛṣabhāṇāṃ varāhāṇāṃ mārjārāṇāṃ tathaiva ca śālāvṛkāṇāṃ pretānāṃ bhuruṇḍānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: — of elephants, sṛmaras, śarabhas of every kind, bulls, boars, cats, and likewise wolves, pretas, and bhuruṇḍa birds of every sort —

sanskrit: gṛdhrāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ ca makarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca piśācānāṃ sayakṣāṇāṃ tathaiva ca suradviṣām
english: — of vultures, Garuḍas, makaras, piśācas along with yakṣas, and likewise the enemies of the gods —

sanskrit: guhyakānāṃ ca saṃgrāme nairṛtānāṃ tathaiva ca jhaṣāṇāṃ gajavaktrāṇām ulūkānāṃ tathaiva ca
english: — of guhyakas in battle and nairṛtas likewise, great fish, elephant-faced beings, and owls —

sanskrit: mīnakūrmasamūhānāṃ nānāśastrāsipāṇinām tathaiva yātu dhānānāṃ gadāmudgaradhāriṇām
english: — multitudes of fish and tortoises bearing various weapons and swords, and yātudhānas wielding clubs and hammers —

sanskrit: etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhir nānārūpadharais tathā sarvam āsīj jagad vyāptaṃ tasminn astre visarjite
english: With these and many others assuming various forms, the entire world was pervaded when that weapon was released.

sanskrit: triṣirobhiś caturdaṃṣṭraiś caturāsyaiś caturbhujaiḥ anekarūpasaṃyuktair māṃsamedovasāśibhiḥ abhīkṣṇaṃ vadhyamānās te dānavā ye samāgatāḥ
english: The Dānavas who had assembled were slaughtered again and again by three-headed, four-fanged, four-faced, four-armed forms of many kinds, feeding on flesh, fat, and marrow.

sanskrit: arkajvalanatejobhir vajrāśanisamaprabhaiḥ adrisāramayaiś cānyair bāṇair arividāraṇaiḥ nyahanaṃ dānavān sarvān muhūrtenaiva bhārata
english: With the blazing energy of the sun, with the radiance of thunderbolts and lightning, with other arrows of iron-hard mountain-stone that rend foes, I slew all the Dānavas in but a moment, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvāstrapraṇunnāṃs tān gatāsūn nabhasaś cyutān dṛṣṭvāhaṃ prāṇamaṃ bhūyas tripuraghnāya vedhase
english: Seeing them struck down by the Gāṇḍīva-weapon, lifeless and fallen from the sky, I bowed again to the Creator who destroyed Tripura.

sanskrit: tathā raudrāstraniṣpiṣṭān divyābharaṇabhūṣitān niśāmya paramaṃ harṣam agamad devasārathiḥ
english: Beholding them crushed by the Raudra weapon, still adorned with their divine ornaments, the divine charioteer was filled with the greatest joy.

sanskrit: tad asahyaṃ kṛtaṃ karma devair api durāsadam dṛṣṭvā māṃ pūjayām āsa mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ
english: Seeing that unbearable feat accomplished — difficult even for the gods to achieve — Matali, the charioteer of Śakra, honoured me.

sanskrit: uvāca cedaṃ vacanaṃ prīyamāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ surāsurair asahyaṃ hi karma yat sādhitaṃ tvayā na hy etat saṃyuge kartum api śaktaḥ sureśvaraḥ
english: Delighted and joining his palms, he spoke these words: "The deed you have accomplished is unbearable even for gods and demons; not even the lord of the gods would be capable of performing this in battle."

sanskrit: surāsurair avadhyaṃ hi puram etat khagaṃ mahat tvayā vimathitaṃ vīra svavīryāstratapobalāt
english: "This great sky-faring city, invincible to gods and demons, has been shattered by you, O hero, through your own strength of valour, weapons, and austerity."

sanskrit: vidhvaste 'tha pure tasmin dānaveṣu hateṣu ca vinadantyaḥ striyaḥ sarvā niṣpetur nagarād bahiḥ
english: When that city was destroyed and the Dānavas slain, all the women rushed out from the city wailing.

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśyo vyathitāḥ kurarya iva duḥkhitāḥ petuḥ putrān pitṝn bhrātṝñ śocamānā mahītale
english: With dishevelled hair, distressed, wretched like osprey-birds, they fell to the earth lamenting their sons, fathers, and brothers.

sanskrit: rudantyo dīnakaṇṭhyas tā vinadantyo hateśvarāḥ urāṃsi pāṇibhir ghnantyaḥ prasrastasragvibhūṣaṇāḥ
english: Weeping with piteous throats, wailing with their lords slain, beating their breasts with their hands, their garlands and ornaments fallen away —

sanskrit: tac chokayuktam aśrīkaṃ duḥkhadainyasamāhatam na babhau dānavapuraṃ hatatviṭkaṃ hateśvaram
english: Stricken with grief, stripped of its glory, battered by sorrow and misery, its lustre extinguished and its lords slain, the Dānava city no longer shone.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraṃ hatanāgam iva hradam śuṣkavṛkṣam ivāraṇyam adṛśyam abhavat puram
english: Like a gandharva city in appearance, like a lake whose great serpent has been slain, like a forest of withered trees, the city became invisible.

sanskrit: māṃ tu saṃhṛṣṭamanasaṃ kṣipraṃ mātalir ānayat devarājasya bhavanaṃ kṛtakarmāṇam āhavāt
english: But Matali, his heart overjoyed, quickly brought me — my task accomplished in battle — to the palace of the king of gods.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapuram ārujya nihatya ca mahāsurān nivātakavacāṃś caiva tato 'haṃ śakram āgamam
english: Having stormed Hiraṇyapura and slain the great asuras and the Nivātakavacas, I then came before Śakra.

sanskrit: mama karma ca devendraṃ mātalir vistareṇa tat sarvaṃ viśrāvayām āsa yathā bhūtaṃ mahādyute
english: And Matali reported all my deeds in full detail to Indra, lord of the gods, exactly as they had occurred, O greatly splendid one.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapuraghātaṃ ca māyānāṃ ca nivāraṇam nivātakavacānāṃ ca vadhaṃ saṃkhye mahaujasām
english: The destruction of Hiraṇyapura, the repulsion of the illusions, and the slaying of the mighty Nivātakavacas in battle —

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhagavān prītaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ marudbhiḥ sahitaḥ śrīmān sādhu sādhv ity athābravīt
english: Hearing this, the blessed thousand-eyed Puraṃdara, glorious and accompanied by the Maruts, then said, "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: tato māṃ devarājo vai samāśvāsya punaḥ punaḥ abravīd vibudhaiḥ sārdham idaṃ sumadhuraṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the king of gods, reassuring me again and again, spoke these very sweet words in the presence of the divine ones.

sanskrit: atidevāsuraṃ karma kṛtam etat tvayā raṇe gurvarthaś ca mahān pārtha kṛtaḥ śatrūn ghnatā mama
english: "This feat performed by you in battle surpasses what gods and asuras could do; a great and weighty service has been rendered to me, O Pārtha, by your slaying of my enemies."

sanskrit: evam eva sadā bhāvyaṃ sthireṇājau dhanaṃjaya asaṃmūḍhena cāstrāṇāṃ kartavyaṃ pratipādanam
english: "Always should you be thus — steady in battle, O Dhanaṃjaya; unconfused in applying the weapons, that is what must be done."

sanskrit: aviṣahyo raṇe hi tvaṃ devadānavarākṣasaiḥ sayakṣāsuragandharvaiḥ sapakṣigaṇapannagaiḥ
english: "In battle you are invincible to gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, to yakṣas with their asura hosts, gandharvas, winged creatures, and serpents."

sanskrit: vasudhāṃ cāpi kaunteya tvadbāhubalanirjitām pālayiṣyati dharmātmā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "And the earth, O son of Kuntī, conquered by the strength of your arms, will be governed by the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tato mām abhiviśvastaṃ saṃrūḍhaśaravikṣatam devarājo 'nugṛhyedaṃ kāle vacanam abravīt
english: Arjuna said: Then, when I was fully recovered and my arrow-wounds had healed, the king of gods graciously spoke these words to me at the proper time.

sanskrit: divyāny astrāṇi sarvāṇi tvayi tiṣṭhanti bhārata na tvābhibhavituṃ śakto mānuṣo bhuvi kaś cana
english: "All the divine weapons reside in you, O Bhārata; no mortal on this earth is capable of overpowering you."

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniḥ saha rājabhiḥ saṃgrāmasthasya te putra kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
english: "Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Śakuni together with their kings — when you stand on the battlefield, my son, they are not worth a sixteenth part of you."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca me tanutrāṇaṃ prāyacchan maghavān prabhuḥ abhedyaṃ kavacaṃ divyaṃ srajaṃ caiva hiraṇmayīm
english: And the mighty Maghavan, lord of all, bestowed on me this protective covering — a divine impenetrable armour and also a golden garland.

sanskrit: devadattaṃ ca me śaṅkhaṃ devaḥ prādān mahāravam divyaṃ cedaṃ kirīṭaṃ me svayam indro yuyoja ha
english: The god also gave me the conch Devadatta with its great sound; and Indra himself placed this divine diadem on my head.

sanskrit: tato divyāni vastrāṇi divyāny ābharaṇāni ca prādāc chakro mamaitāni rucirāṇi bṛhanti ca
english: Then Śakra gave me these divine garments and divine ornaments — splendid and magnificent.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃpūjitas tatra sukham asmy uṣito nṛpa indrasya bhavane puṇye gandharvaśiśubhiḥ saha
english: Thus honoured, I dwelt happily there, O king, in the sacred palace of Indra, together with the young Gandharvas.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīc chakraḥ prītimān amaraiḥ saha samayo 'rjuna gantuṃ te bhrātaro hi smaranti te
english: Then Śakra, delighted, spoke to me in the presence of the immortals: "The time has come for you to go, Arjuna — your brothers remember you."

sanskrit: evam indrasya bhavane pañca varṣāṇi bhārata uṣitāni mayā rājan smaratā dyūtajaṃ kalim
english: Thus five years were spent by me in the palace of Indra, O Bhārata, O king, all the while remembering the quarrel born of the dice-game.

sanskrit: tato bhavantam adrākṣaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritam gandhamādanam āsādya parvatasyāsya mūrdhani
english: Then I saw you, surrounded by your brothers, having reached Gandhamādana, on the summit of this very mountain.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca diṣṭyā dhanaṃjayāstrāṇi tvayā prāptāni bhārata diṣṭyā cārādhito rājā devānām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By good fortune have the weapons been obtained by you, O Dhanaṃjaya, O Bhārata; by good fortune the king, lord and master of the gods, has been propitiated.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca bhagavān sthāṇur devyā saha paraṃtapa sākṣād dṛṣṭaḥ suyuddhena toṣitaś ca tvayānagha
english: By good fortune the blessed Sthāṇu together with the Goddess was directly seen, O scorcher of foes, and pleased by your valiant combat, O sinless one.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca lokapālais tvaṃ sameto bharatarṣabha diṣṭyā vardhāmahe sarve diṣṭyāsi punarāgataḥ
english: By good fortune you have met the world-guardians, O bull of the Bhāratas; by good fortune we all prosper; by good fortune you have returned.

sanskrit: adya kṛtsnām imāṃ devīṃ vijitāṃ puramālinīm manye ca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrān api vaśīkṛtān
english: Today I consider this whole divine earth with its garlanded cities to be conquered, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra too to be subdued.

sanskrit: tāni tv icchāmi te draṣṭuṃ divyāny astrāṇi bhārata yais tathā vīryavantas te nivātakavacā hatā
english: But I desire to see those divine weapons of yours, O Bhārata, with which those mighty Nivātakavacas were slain.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca śvaḥ prabhāte bhavān draṣṭā divyāny astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ nivātakavacā ghorā yair mayā vinipātitāḥ
english: Arjuna said: Tomorrow at dawn you shall see all the divine weapons with which those terrible Nivātakavacas were struck down by me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam āgamanaṃ tatra kathayitvā dhanaṃjayaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvai rajanīṃ tām uvāsa ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus narrated his arrival there, Dhanaṃjaya spent that night together with all his brothers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ utthāyāvaśyakāryāṇi kṛtavān bhratṛbhiḥ saha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When that night had passed, the dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira rose and performed his necessary duties together with his brothers.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcodayām āsa so 'rjunaṃ bhrātṛnandanam darśayāstrāṇi kaunteya yair jitā dānavās tvayā
english: Then he urged Arjuna, the joy of his brothers: "Show the weapons, O son of Kuntī, with which you conquered the Dānavas."

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayo rājan devair dattāni pāṇḍavaḥ astrāṇi tāni divyāni darśayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, that Pāṇḍava, O king, displayed those divine weapons bestowed by the gods, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yathānyāyaṃ mahātejāḥ śaucaṃ paramam āsthitaḥ girikūbaraṃ pādapāṅgaṃ śubhaveṇu triveṇukam pārthivaṃ ratham āsthāya śobhamāno dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The greatly radiant Dhanaṃjaya, observing supreme ritual purity in the proper manner, mounting the earthly chariot with its mountain-axle, its tree-staff, its auspicious triple-bamboo triveṇu pole, shone with magnificence.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudaṃśitas tena kavacena suvarcasā dhanur ādāya gāṇḍīvaṃ devadattaṃ ca vārijam
english: Then, well-armoured with that resplendent armour, taking up the Gāṇḍīva bow and the conch Devadatta born of the waters —
